apertura: How many high-card points do you generally need to open?
A normal one-level opening generally starts around 12-13 HCP. Pre-empts and distributional exceptions require separate evaluation.
atout: In a 4♥ contract, which wins between ♥3 and ♠A?
♥3 if played as a ruff: hearts are trumps
It depends on who plays first
A heart legally played as a ruff beats any non-trump card, including an ace.
attacco: The defender to declarer's left makes the opening lead.
bilanciata: A 6-3-2-2 hand has a six-card suit and two doubletons. The balanced shapes taught here are 4-3-3-3, 4-4-3-2 and 5-3-3-2; a single doubleton does not itself make a hand unbalanced.
caduta: If declarer takes seven tricks in 3NT, how many undertricks are there?
3NT requires nine tricks. Seven tricks means two down: 9 minus 7.
contare: What should you count during play?
Cards played in each suit, to know what remains
Counting the cards played helps you work out the remaining distribution and choose a line of play.
contratto: How many tricks must declarer take in 3♠?
Add the bid level to the six-trick book: 3♠ requires nine tricks with spades as trumps.
contro: What does doubling an opposing contract change?
Contract trick points are doubled and special bonuses or penalties apply
A double doubles contract trick points, not every scoring item. A made doubled contract has additional bonuses; undertricks use the doubled penalty scale.
cue_bid: With an agreed trump fit, what is the purpose of a control bid when exploring slam?
To show a control, such as an ace or void
A control bid shows first- or second-round control, depending on the agreement, to investigate slam. Bidding the opponents' suit can have other meanings in other auctions.
dichiarante: The player who makes the last bid
The partner with the most points
The player on the declaring side who first bid the final denomination
Declarer is the player in the winning partnership who first bid the suit or notrump denomination of the final contract.
difensori: How many tricks must the defenders win to defeat 4♠?
4♠ requires ten tricks. Four defensive tricks leave declarer with at most nine.
distribuzione: What is the shape of a hand with five spades, four hearts, three diamonds and one club?
The shape is 5-4-3-1. These numbers describe the suit lengths in descending order.
ducking: Why deliberately lose a trick by ducking?
To give the opponents a gift
To preserve entries while establishing a long suit
Ducking can preserve access to the hand containing the long suit, allowing its established cards to be cashed later.
eliminazione: What is the principle of an endplay?
Force an opponent to make a favourable lead for you
An endplay leaves an opponent on lead with no safe exit: their next play gives you an advantage.
fit: How many combined cards in one suit normally constitute a fit?
A fit normally means at least eight cards in the suit between the two partners.
forzante: What does a forcing bid mean?
Partner must keep bidding and cannot pass
A forcing bid requires partner to continue the auction rather than pass, within the agreed forcing conditions.
hold_up: What is the purpose of a hold-up in notrump?
Pretend not to hold the ace
Exhaust one defender's cards in the led suit to break communications
Holding up can exhaust the led suit in one defender's hand, so that defender cannot continue it after gaining the lead.
impasse: What is the aim of a finesse?
Gain a trick by playing towards an honour when an opposing honour is favourably placed
A finesse tries to gain a trick from the favourable location of an opposing honour, for example by leading towards AQ when hoping the king is onside.
libro: How many tricks make up the book?
The book is six tricks. Add the bid level: 1♠ requires 6 plus 1, or seven tricks.
licita: What happens if all four players pass at their first turn?
The hand is played in notrump
The board is passed out: no contract is played
The auction ends without a contract. In duplicate bridge the board is scored as passed out; it is not redealt for the other tables.
manche: Which undoubled contract is NOT game?
2♠ is a partscore. The lowest undoubled game contracts are 3NT, 4♥, 4♠, 5♣ and 5♦.
mano: How many cards does each player receive?
The 52-card deck is divided equally among four players: thirteen cards each.
mazziere: What is dealer's role at the start?
Deal the cards and make the first call
Dealer distributes the cards and has the first turn to call in the auction.
morto: When does dummy expose their cards?
After the defender to declarer's left makes the opening lead
Dummy exposes their cards after the opening lead, not before it.
onori: Ace, king, queen, jack and ten
The five honours are A, K, Q, J and 10. Only A, K, Q and J have Milton Work HCP values; the ten is worth zero HCP.
parziale: Which undoubled contract is a partscore?
Undoubled 2♠ is below game. The lowest game contracts are 3NT, 4♥, 4♠, 5♣ and 5♦.
presa: The highest card in the suit led, or the highest trump if any are played
The player with the longest suit
The player with the most HCP
The highest trump wins if any trump is played; otherwise the highest card in the suit led wins.
presa_perdente: How can you eliminate a loser?
By a finesse, a ruff or discarding it on a winner
Losers can be eliminated through a finesse, a ruff in dummy or a discard on a winning card.
presa_sicura: At notrump, what makes a card a sure winner?
Being the highest remaining card in its suit
The highest remaining card in a suit wins when that suit is played at notrump, provided the hand can be reached to cash it.
punti_distribuzione: In the shortage-point scheme shown here, how many points is a singleton worth?
In this scheme, used to revalue a hand with a trump fit: void 3, singleton 2, doubleton 1. These are not HCP.
punti_onore: How many HCP is a king worth?
Milton Work HCP: ace 4, king 3, queen 2, jack 1. Tens have no HCP value.
regola_venti: Add HCP and the lengths of the two longest suits; 20 suggests an opening
Hold at least twenty high cards
If HCP plus the lengths of the two longest suits reaches twenty, opening with fewer than twelve HCP may be considered. It is a guideline, not an obligation.
rientro: To reach the hand whose winners you need to cash
Entries let you transfer the lead to the hand containing the winners you want to cash.
risposta: What does responder communicate to opener?
Strength and distribution, including any fit
Responses describe strength and shape to help the partnership find a suitable contract.
ruff: Why can ruffing in dummy gain tricks when dummy has shorter trumps?
It adds tricks without shortening declarer's longer trumps
Ruffing with the shorter trump holding can create extra tricks while preserving declarer's longer trumps.
scarto: What is the difference between a ruff and a discard?
A ruff uses a trump; a discard is an off-suit non-trump card
Ruffs occur only on the first trick
When unable to follow suit, playing a trump is a ruff; playing a non-trump card of another suit is a discard.
segnale: Under a high-encouraging attitude agreement, what does a high defensive spot card suggest?
I have no cards left in this suit
With this attitude agreement, high encourages and low discourages. Count, suit-preference and other signalling methods have different meanings.
seme_lungo: From how many cards is a suit normally called long?
A long suit normally contains at least five cards and may provide extra tricks once established.
senza_atout: At notrump, what happens if you cannot follow suit?
You may ruff with another suit
You must discard and cannot win that trick
There are no trumps at notrump. If void in the suit led, you must discard a card of another suit, which cannot win the trick.
slam: How many tricks does a small slam require?
A small slam is a six-level contract requiring twelve tricks. A grand slam requires all thirteen.
sottomano: Why is playing low in second hand often useful?
To conserve honours for a more effective play later
Second hand low is a guideline for conserving honours, not an absolute rule; the position may require playing high.
squeeze: A defender must guard more suits than their remaining cards allow
A squeeze forces a defender to abandon a guard because they cannot keep enough cards to protect all the relevant suits.
stayman: Whether partner has a four-card major
Exactly how many HCP partner has
Whether partner wants to play notrump
Stayman asks about four-card majors to look for a 4-4 heart or spade fit.
surtaglio: Ruffing a second time in the same trick
Playing a higher trump than a previous ruff in the trick
An overruff uses a trump higher than the trump already played as a ruff in that trick.
sviluppo: What does it mean to establish a suit?
Remove opposing high cards so that remaining lower cards become winners
Change the trump suit during play
Establishing a suit promotes lower cards into winners, for example by driving out opposing high cards.
taglio: When void in the suit led and holding a trump
Only with the ace of trumps
You may ruff only when you cannot follow the suit led. Playing a trump may win the trick, unless a higher trump is played.
terza_alta: What does the guideline third hand high suggest?
Play the lowest card in third position
Play high enough in third position to try to win or force an opposing honour
Third hand generally plays high to win or force an honour. Use the lowest of touching equals; the layout may create exceptions.
transfer: Using Jacoby transfers after 1NT, what does 2♦ mean?
Please bid 2♥: I have long hearts
2♦ asks opener to bid 2♥. If hearts become trumps, opener will be declarer and responder, who made the transfer, will be dummy.
vulnerabile: What changes when a partnership is vulnerable?
Game and slam bonuses and undertrick penalties are higher
Vulnerability increases game and slam bonuses and undertrick penalties; it does not change every scoring item.
